title.narrative: Integrated Natural Resources and Environmental Management Project

description.narrative: The project will address unsustainable watershed management in four priority river basins of the country. The project will be implemented as a sector loan to institutionalize effective watershed management regimes in four upper river basins (URBs) that can be replicated across the country. The four URBs are (i) Chico River Basin in Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR), Northern Luzon island, (ii) Wahig-Inabanga on the island of Bohol, (iii) Lake Lanao Basin in the Autonomous Region of Muslim Mindanao (ARMM) and Upper Bukidnon River Basin in Bukidnon (the latter two on the island of Mindanao).

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Increased rural household incomes and LGU revenues in selected watersheds in the four URBs.

By 2020: Rural household incomes in project areas increased by 30% from 2009 levels (P60,000-90,000 per annum) Progress/Status: From draft PCR, household Survey conducted in late 2023 shows that average total household income increased by 37% from 2009 to 2021. On the other hand, the Socio-Economic Survey done earlier in 2021 shows that household income rose by as much as 75%, although rates of increased varied across locations. Data Source: Income class ranking of river basin LGUs and households in IPO areas
BLGF's income classification of LGUs (every 4 years).
NSO and NSCB census and poverty data
DENR-RBCO and NEDA annual reports
Project monitoring reports generated under RBCO management system. Actual value:

Revenues of participating municipalities in the URBs increased by 10% from 2010 income levels (ranging from 30 to 105 million pesos) through project investments in livelihood, biodiversity protection and conservation, and PES. Progress/Status: From the draft PCR, the LGU Revenue Generation Assessment showed that among many possible sources of local revenues, four sources are most likely to be impacted by INREMP investments: (1) regulatory fees, (2) service and user charges, (3) business taxes, and (4) real property taxes.
Extrapolating from the assessment results, the target 10% increase in LGU revenues has been achieved in most of the 91 LGUs covered by the project. The table 11 in the draft PCR showed that the target 10% revenue increase was met in most of the 21 out of the 23 sample LGUs based on the nominal value of revenues. Deflating the end-of-project revenues to the baseline year 2010, the 10% increase was achieved in 19 sample LGUs. Data Source: Income class ranking of river basin LGUs and households in IPO areas

Poverty incidence rate in the project areas decreased to 25% from 47% (2009 baseline) Progress/Status: From the draft PCR, official Government data from the Philippine Statistic Authority showed that poverty incidence in the INREMP provinces has been declining and that among the nine provinces covered by the project, poverty incidence is now within the target level of 25%.
